SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

nm south of C Tower to near S Tower to 10 nm south of V Tower,

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.description:
A series of low pressure systems will move through the panhandle
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the light rain will continue Saturday evening before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday night into Sunday
morning bringing moderate to heavy rain fall. Rain showers will
then take over on Sunday that may bring occasional moderate to
heavy rainfall as well.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.

properties.description:

with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy
showers and thunderstorms dropping south early in the week.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Levy and Marion
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to hold steady at flood stage.
Additional rises are possible.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
